items.title: [cbc.ca] B.C. floods force evacuations, shelter orders as roads close
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Heavy rain and flooding across British Columbia’s South Coast prompted shelter-in-place advisories near Squamish and in Pemberton Valley, while evacuation orders covered parts of Pemberton and Lil’wat Nation on Thursday, Nov. 12. Some areas received more than 300 millimetres of rain in 48 hours, and floodwater closed Highway 99 east of Pemberton and roads near Squamish. The entire Village of Pemberton was under an evacuation alert. Evacuation orders also remained in effect in Zeballos, where flooding and landslide risks threatened about 30 properties. The release of water from the Cheakamus Dam flooded roads near Squamish and was intended to make room in the reservoir for more rain. Officials expected river levels to crest Thursday and then recede. Rain eased in some areas, but Vancouver Island remained under rainfall and flood warnings, and forecasters were tracking more storm systems expected over the weekend.

items.title: [tsln.com] Cattle specialists urge targeted winter feeding to manage costs
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Cattle advisers and researchers are urging producers to match winter rations to forage quality and herd needs. Drought has tightened forage supplies, and feed is a major operating expense. South Dakota State University research found that limit-fed, energy-dense diets reduced feed use and methane emissions without harming calf growth through weaning, saving about $29 per cow. Kansas State University cow-calf specialist Jason Warner recommends assessing forage and supplementing protein as dormant grasses lose quality. French livestock trainer Guillaume Beaure describes reducing feed waste by closely matching rations to animals’ needs. Advisers also recommend checking forage mineral levels because winter hay can pose a risk of magnesium deficiency.

items.title: [winnipegfreepress.com] Federal memo warns freshwater pressures threaten Canada’s long-term security
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

An internal federal memo warns that growing pressure on freshwater supplies could harm Canada’s long-term security and prosperity. It says it is unclear whether the country can meet future needs as its cities and economy grow. The Canada Water Agency prepared the document for Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin as work proceeds on a national water security strategy. Dabrusin called the strategy a “mission critical priority” in response to Prime Minister Mark Carney’s request for cabinet priorities. The memo links water risks to climate change, pollution, population growth, overuse and aging infrastructure. Public consultation ran from Sept. 9 to Oct. 25, and the agency also consulted provincial, territorial and Indigenous partners. The memo calls for an assessment of water protection and sustainable management, including shared waters with the United States and global water risks. The 12-page memo was obtained through an access-to-information request, with some material withheld.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

A groundbreaking drone survey has revealed a startling split in the fate of New Zealand's endangered Erect-crested penguins. While one population has remained stable for decades, another has declined by more than 40%, apparently due to a combination of predators, worsening storms, and changing ocean conditions. Even more surprisingly, the tiny Bounty Islands support nearly as many breeding pairs as the Antipodes Islands, despite being 40 times smaller.

items.title: [thesouthafrican.com] WMO warns strengthening El Niño could intensify global extremes into 2027
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says a strengthening El Niño could reach record strength by December and intensify heat and disruptive rainfall patterns into 2027. In its 2026 climate update, the agency reported that global temperatures from January through September averaged about 1.47°C above the preindustrial level and said 2026 is on track to rank among the four warmest years on record. Human-caused warming is adding to the risks associated with the naturally occurring climate pattern. The World Health Organization (WHO) has classified the expected health effects as an emergency for the first time for an El Niño event and published a plan for a Grade 3 preparedness response requiring major to maximal efforts. The agency warns that heat, drought and heavy rain can increase risks of heat illness, food insecurity and infectious disease, with vulnerable and conflict-affected communities facing particular danger. The WMO says the event is on track to reach record strength by December; its climate update uses data through September and does not include the latest impacts.

Turkey is promoting a goal to increase electricity’s share of global energy demand from about 20% to 35% by 2035. Developed countries have resisted further funding commitments, and the Trump administration is not taking part in negotiations.

Leaders of the United States, India, Japan and Australia agreed at a Manila summit on Nov. 17 to expand cooperation on maritime surveillance, cybersecurity, undersea cables and counterterrorism, and to establish the Quad’s first Business Leaders’ Forum in Mumbai in early 2027. The meeting was the first in-person Quad leaders’ summit since September 2024 and U.S. President Donald Trump’s first in his current term. The summit took place ahead of Trump’s scheduled Nov. 19 meetings in Shenzhen with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The Quad’s export credit agencies were due to meet in Tokyo on Nov. 18 to discuss financing joint projects.

items.title: [frontpageafricaonline.com] COP31 draft proposes $120 billion in annual adaptation finance by 2035
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

A draft COP31 agreement proposes at least $120 billion a year in adaptation finance for developing countries by 2035, alongside accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels. Released by the conference presidency on Nov. 16, the text remains under negotiation and does not represent an agreed position; the talks in Antalya, Türkiye, are scheduled to end Nov. 20. African negotiators are pressing for predictable grants, measurable delivery milestones and finance that does not deepen debt. The United Nations Environment Programme estimates developing countries will need $305 billion annually for adaptation by 2035, while international public adaptation finance reached $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion in 2024. Ghanaian Environment Minister Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings also called for funding to restore land and rivers damaged by mining and for greater local processing of Africa’s minerals.

items.title: [livescience.com] NASA's Swift telescope burns up after nearly 22 years
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory reentered Earth’s atmosphere and burned up over North Sumatra on Nov. 4, ending a nearly 22-year mission. Its observations, including millions of images, remain available for research. A 24-hour ultraviolet exposure of the Andromeda galaxy was assembled from observations made between May and July 2008. NASA said Swift detected about 20,000 ultraviolet sources there, many of them hot stars and star clusters obscured in visible-light views. Swift was designed to turn rapidly toward short-lived cosmic explosions and observe them in optical, ultraviolet and X-ray light. It also alerted other observatories so they could follow events before they faded. The U.S. Space Force said Swift reentered the atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST over North Sumatra. NASA expected most of the spacecraft to burn up, though some pieces may have survived.

The European Space Agency’s (ESA) Hera spacecraft has arrived near the Didymos asteroid pair and begun surveying Dimorphos, the smaller body NASA struck in its 2022 DART asteroid-deflection test. Hera is gathering initial observations from about 25 to 30 kilometers away. Researchers want to establish whether the collision left a crater or reshaped the asteroid and determine its mass and composition. The impact shortened Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, but scientists still need to explain why the change was so large and how the asteroid responded. Hera is expected to begin closer observations in December, with further images and findings scheduled for presentation on November 25.

Full-size 3D-printed tungsten tiles survived 74 plasma discharges inside the DIII-D National Fusion Facility in San Diego, remaining intact after about four minutes of total plasma exposure over three days. Researchers from North Carolina State University, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Japanese manufacturer JEOL made the tiles using electron-beam powder bed fusion, keeping the tungsten powder bed above 1,400°C during printing to limit cracking. The parts still await detailed erosion and surface analysis after a radiation survey.

items.content_html:

The Federal Aviation Administration plans to replace four aging information systems that rely on floppy disks with a unified digital platform at 435 air traffic facilities by the end of 2028. The new Enterprise Information Display System, or E-IDS, will consolidate weather alerts, airport status and flight notices that controllers currently retrieve through outdated, often manual processes. The FAA is seeking additional funding through the proposed Modern Skies Act. The agency plans to deploy the system at the remaining locations by the end of 2028.

items.title: [medicalxpress.com] Study links very large and small waists to higher death risk
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

A study of more than 17 million South Korean adults found that both unusually large and unusually small waist measurements were associated with a higher risk of death across weight and age groups. The lowest observed risk was associated with waist circumferences of 80–94 centimeters in men and 75–89 centimeters in women. The association between waist circumference and death risk was stronger at older ages, especially among women 75 and older. Researchers analyzed routine health-check measurements from 2009–10 and tracked survival for nearly 14 years, through June 30, 2024. The study was observational and cannot show that waist size causes death. Among people with normal weight or overweight whose waist circumference was high for their body mass index (BMI), reducing waist circumference without necessarily losing weight appeared to offer a greater survival benefit than losing weight while reducing waist circumference, the authors said.

Hosting provider OVHcloud says it deployed official fixes or its own backports across all 15 PHP versions on its shared-hosting platform, covering more than 6 million websites on about 5,000 servers. The fixes address two PHP flaws collectively known as PHP2Shell that can let attackers run commands on vulnerable servers without credentials. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has confirmed active exploitation and set an Oct. 29 deadline for federal civilian agencies to address the flaws. Censys’ tracker showed more than 10 million services patched since Oct. 21, while a scan found more than 4 million services in Germany still reporting vulnerable PHP version numbers. The scanner cautions that backported fixes may not appear in those version strings. OVHcloud says it wrote fixes for PHP 5.3 through 7.3, versions the PHP project no longer maintains. Researchers documented 35 shell executions on three deliberately vulnerable honeypots, but the test used a favorable single-worker setup. CISA has not named affected organizations or described the evidence behind its listing, and the designation does not establish the scale of successful compromises in production. Some earlier claims of successful exploitation were withdrawn or qualified after investigators found scanning or could not confirm PHP2Shell as the entry point.

It called for coordinated infection prevention, careful antibiotic prescribing, stronger laboratory capacity and surveillance. Faster genomic monitoring can help track the spread of resistant strains and guide treatment decisions, it said.

items.title: [yna.co.kr] Lenders scrutinize AI borrowing as stock selloff curbs financing appetite
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Banks and credit investors are scrutinizing artificial-intelligence borrowing more closely and are reluctant to finance new deals after a technology selloff erased $2.5 trillion in Nasdaq 100 market value on Thursday and intensified questions about data-center growth. Some lenders have hesitated even when deals carry guarantees from major technology companies, while bank HSBC said the stock decline appeared excessive and argued that regulation could slow, but not derail, AI infrastructure spending. Lenders are concerned that political resistance could slow data-center construction and that AI investments may not generate returns quickly enough to support the debt. South Korean shares rebounded on Nov. 10 as investors reassessed the regulatory risk, but lenders are stress-testing project cash flows and customer contracts. AI developer Anthropic aims to begin trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19 or 20 in an offering that could raise about $100 billion.

items.title: [cbsnews.com] Trump and Marcos announce trade deal before planned Xi-Putin talks
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

President Donald Trump and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced a trade deal in Manila on Wednesday, ahead of Trump’s planned talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday. Trump called it a major agreement, but the leaders did not publicly detail its terms. The announcement followed Trump’s Manila meetings with Southeast Asian leaders and the first summit in two years of the Quad, which comprises the United States, Japan, India and Australia. The Quad’s joint statement expressed concern over economic coercion and arbitrary export restrictions without naming a country. Leaders also outlined maritime patrol exercises for 2027 and continued cooperation on an artificial-intelligence accelerator. Trump said the Quad would invest more than $85 million to expand access to trusted AI ecosystems across the Indo-Pacific. Trump’s brief visit to the Philippines also drew protests over his policies and Pax Silica, a U.S.-led supply-chain initiative. Human Rights Watch said police detained at least 245 protesters, including farmers, journalists and children. Trump is due to travel to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit and the scheduled three-leader meeting on Nov. 19.

items.title: [thestar.com] Supreme Court hears challenge to Canada’s ban on 2,500 firearm types
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

The Supreme Court of Canada began hearing a challenge Monday to the federal ban on more than 2,500 types of firearms the government classifies as assault-style weapons. The appeal follows two lower-court defeats for gun owners, advocacy groups and businesses challenging cabinet’s authority to prohibit the guns through regulations. The ban includes some firearms used for hunting and sport shooting. The government prohibited 1,500 models and variants, including the AR-15 and Ruger Mini-14, in May 2020 and later expanded the list. Federal lawyers argue cabinet acted reasonably to address public-safety risks, while appellants say the regulations exceeded the authority Parliament granted and failed to account for lawful sporting and hunting uses. The hearings continue Tuesday, and a decision is expected by the end of 2027 at the latest. The possession amnesty runs until 90 days after the court rules.
